items.title: 美国中期选举蓝潮冲击 AI 行业，44 项数据中心暂停提案中 43 项通过
items.description: 美国中期选举民主党拿下参众两院，多场竞选以问责 AI 公司为主题，行业面临监管、数据中心建设放缓等前景。44 项地方数据中心暂停提案中 43 项通过，NBC 民调显示 76% 选民反对在社区建数据中心；专家称共和党禁止州级 AI 限制的尝试可能终结，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 未置评，据华尔街日报报道 CEO 们在私下讨论算力容量受限问题。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/vkfrtci1ufbtbydsqersys6lx

items.title: 腾讯姚顺雨谈“AI 模型公司护城河”：更多存在于产品层，而不是模型层
items.description: IT之家 11 月 8 日消息，据第一财经报道，在 2026 未来科学大奖的一场对话中，清华大学讲席教授、中国工程院外籍院士张亚勤向腾讯首席 AI 科学家姚顺雨抛出了一个尖锐的商业问题， 模型公司的护城河究竟是什么 ？ 姚顺雨的回答是， AI 护城河更多存在于产品层，而不是模型层 。真正难以替代的，不一定是最聪明的模型，而是能够理解用户背景、利用专有数据和上下文，并获得用户信任的 AI 产品。 姚顺雨以微信为例，如果用户可以直接在微信中使用 AI，这个 AI 未必需要拥有最强大的模型能力，但它了解用户的日程安排、朋友关系和各种活动信息。这些信息能够帮助 AI 更好地理解用户需要什么，也使其他模型难以直接替代它。即使竞争对手推出了一个更聪明的模型，也不意味着它能够提供同样的服务，因为后者未必知道用户是谁。 听完这一回答，张亚勤调侃道，按照姚顺雨的逻辑，Anthropic 未来或许不值一万亿甚至两万亿美元，因为模型终有一天可能走向商品化。随后，张亚勤又笑着提醒现场的学生，千万不要听自己的建议去买股票。 IT之家注：姚顺雨本科毕业于清华大学姚班，获普林斯顿大学计算机科学博士学位，2024 年

Democrats’ historic victory in this week’s midterm elections could also have a dramatic effect on the tech industry. In dozens of local ballot measures, voters rejected data centers . A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The New York Times, which had previously said Nvidia’s chief executive had been the target of Chinese intelligence, was the first to report on the memo , which was reportedly based on U.S. intelligence. Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets. The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities. Microsoft has previously described Artex as a system of AI agents that can conduct cyberattacks “from reconnaissance through data exfiltration with little needed human interaction.” In a blog post , cybersecurity firm Censys, which scans the internet for exposed or vulnerable systems, said that it identified more than 800 distinct deployments of Artex that were accessible from the web without needing a password to log in. Silas Cutler, principal security researcher at Censys who wrote the blog post, said that not every instance of Artex is operated maliciously and many are used for authorized testers

Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it. A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month. As Anthropic gears up for its IPO , the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed. “Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch. “That’s fine as long as AI spend continues to rise, but if it starts to slow down because of something in the market or some other factor, they will all start to slow down simultaneously, and that could lead to other cascading effects.”

Amazon is jumping on the currently most popular bandwagon for interacting with AI agents: texting. The company on Friday said it is launching a feature that lets customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to help them shop, much like you can with AI agents like Muse or Instinct. The move comes after Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse from querying its site in September. The company is rolling the features out just before the start of the holiday shopping season. The e-commerce giant said select U.S. customers will get a text asking them to enable the shopping feature. Those with access can text Alexa to shop on Amazon using natural language queries, spanning everything from searching for items, adding them to cart, and purchasing. The text agent builds on the recent shopping-focused upgrades to Alexa , and so can manage lists, keep tabs on prices, search for items across the web, compare products, and check the status of orders.
